framework.summary: Large frontier developers must write, follow and publish a frontier AI framework and review it at least once a year.
framework.quote: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a frontier AI framework

transparency_report.summary: Frontier developers must publish a transparency report before or when deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model; large developers add risk assessment summaries.
transparency_report.quote: a frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a transparency report

incident_reporting.summary: Frontier developers must report critical safety incidents to the Department of Justice within 15 days of discovery.
incident_reporting.quote: to the department within fifteen days after discovering the critical safety incident

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: Incidents posing imminent risk of death, serious injury or an active cyberattack on critical infrastructure must be disclosed within 24 hours.
imminent_risk_reporting.quote: poses an imminent risk of death, serious physical injury, or an active cyberattack on critical infrastructure, the frontier developer shall disclose that incident within twenty-four hours

third_party_audit.summary: From July 1, 2028, large frontier developers must hire an independent auditor each year to certify compliance with their framework and publish a summary within 30 days.
third_party_audit.quote: a large frontier developer shall retain a third-party auditor to produce a report signed

whistleblower.summary: Frontier developers may not block or retaliate against covered employees who report catastrophic risk or violations; large developers need an anonymous internal reporting process.
whistleblower.quote: enter into any policy or contract that prevents a covered employee from, or retaliates against a covered employee for, making a protected disclosure

registration.summary: The bill sets no registration or licensing requirement.

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown or kill-switch capability.

compute_threshold.summary: A frontier model is one trained with more than 10^26 operations, including fine-tuning, or distilled from one at a compute cost over $5,000,000.
compute_threshold.quote: Was trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10^26

revenue_threshold.summary: A large frontier developer, with its affiliates, had more than five hundred million dollars in annual gross revenues in the preceding calendar year.
revenue_threshold.quote: had more than five hundred million dollars in annual gross

harm_threshold.summary: Catastrophic risk means death or serious injury of more than 50 people or more than $1,000,000,000 in property damage from a single incident.
harm_threshold.quote: the death or serious injury of more than fifty

penalties.summary: The Attorney General may sue large frontier developers for civil penalties up to $1,000,000 for a first violation and $10,000,000 for later violations of the same requirement.
penalties.quote: a penalty not to exceed one million dollars per violation for a first violation or ten million dollars for a second or subsequent violation of the same requirement

effective_date.summary: The Act becomes effective on January 1, 2027.
effective_date.quote: This Act shall become effective on January 1, 2027.

notes: Text cross-references (e.g. R.S. 51:3111.2(F), 3111.5) are misnumbered in the bill itself. Whistleblower section cites 51:3112.
